_meta.probe: P4 — brevity bias across compression surfaces
_meta.finding: Memory truncation is a non-issue (2.5% over the ceiling). Document truncation is severe: 0.65% of 56.5 MB of body text is embedded. But the bulk of that mass is raw conversation dumps that were deliberately unwired from the ingest path, so the fix is selective chunking plus a separate decision about those, not blanket chunking.

memories_vs_512_token_ceiling.verdict: NOT a problem. 2.5% of memories exceed ~512 tokens. Chunking the memories table is not justified; leave the truncation.

documents.verdict: Severe, but not uniformly. 683 of 1081 documents are raw conversation dumps (session-archive, transcript, session) carrying ~40 MB of the 56.5 MB. auto_archive_pending was deliberately unwired from SessionEnd because it produced a searchable pile of conversation rather than facts — chunking those would embed exactly what that decision rejected. The 398 remaining docs (mostly `plan`, avg 3.6 KB body / 184-char summary, 5% embedded) are real knowledge and are the ones worth chunking.

other_surfaces.note: Not measured here. The injection preview is already known to depress the reuse metric in real-usage-report.md; measuring it properly needs a can-you-identify-it-from-the-preview judgement, not a length query.
